## 1. Lawmakers unveiled the 2027 fiscal plan.

The package set revenue at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 6,180 billion</span> and spending at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 7,673 billion</span>, implying a deficit of <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">3.8% of GDP</span> before disaster outlays. Interest payments were projected at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 2,643 billion</span>, equal to roughly Rs. 43 of every Rs. 100 in revenue.

Capital spending was placed at Rs. 2,000 billion, or 5.12% of GDP when the separate Rs. 260 billion Ditwah rebuilding estimate is added. New measures included VAT relief for books, higher public-sector allowances, a Rs. 3.2 billion urban flood program, and removal of the 10% PAL (Port and Airport Development Levy) on imported solar batteries.

The plan also revised border taxes, trimming SCL (Special Commodity Levy) on selected foods while raising the charge on sugar by Rs. 10 per kilo. The document targeted flood-mitigation works in Colombo and suburbs and set aside funds to keep the first terminal operating above design capacity until the second terminal breaks ground.

## 2. A multilateral lender approved $300m for water and sanitation projects.

The ADB (Asian Development Bank) cleared $200 million for climate‑resilient systems in the west and south and sewerage upgrades for about 250,000 people in <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Jaffna</span>. A second $100 million subprogram backed sector reforms on <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">tariffs, governance and private finance</span>.

More than <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">1.3 million people</span> stood to gain improved access to safe drinking water, with new plants, networks, reservoirs and wastewater facilities in scope. The package also funded loss reduction, renewable energy use, and capacity building at the NWSDB (National Water Supply and Drainage Board).

## 3. A security partner provided Rs. 2.08bn for 25 patrol boats.

The grant of <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">JPY 1 billion</span> under the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">OSA (Official Security Assistance) 2026</span> program financed rigid-hull inflatable craft for coastal commands. Officials said the package followed drones supplied in 2025 and would support law enforcement, HADR (<span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">humanitarian assistance and disaster response</span>) and wider maritime surveillance.

Deployment was planned across northern, eastern, northwestern, western and southern areas to deter illegal activity at sea. The note exchange was signed by the Treasury and the embassy, with the Defence Ministry coordinating implementation.

## 4. Bond yields eased as the weekly bill sale missed its target.

Long bonds in the 2030–2036 sector traded between 11.05% and 12.10% as secondary‑market levels slipped. The T‑bill auction raised <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 79.1 billion</span> against a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 90.0 billion</span> offer, with the 3‑month WAYR flat at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">9.35%</span>, the 6‑month down 1 bp to 9.43%, and the 12‑month unchanged at 9.95%.

On FX, the rupee firmed to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 332.35 per US dollar</span> from Rs. 332.56 the prior day. Market volumes were described as moderate while the PDMO (Public Debt Management Office) accepted more short‑end paper than offered in the three‑month line.

## 5. Auditors flagged Rs. 30bn owed by university staff over broken bonds.

A legislative committee disclosed that lecturers who breached agreements faced recovery, with one case seeking to claw back <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 3,633,900</span> after a return from politics. Missing personnel files, evaded attendance scans by <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">38 non‑academic staff</span>, and <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 99,181,457</span> in excess leave payments were also recorded.

## 6. MPs pressed for mandatory standards on imported electric cars and batteries.

A sectoral oversight body heard that <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">NERDC</span> (National Engineering Research and Development Centre) can test capacity, durability and lifespan but noted no compulsory rules exist for EVs, cells, controllers or chargers. The session also raised R&D staffing shortages, a call for better pay, a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">conversion‑to‑electric</span> framework, and a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">petty‑patent proposal</span> to speed commercialisation.

## 7. Officials said 129mm fell in an hour and ordered a joint emergency push.

City engineers told a review that drains were built for roughly <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">30mm per hour</span> and had been <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">blocked by waste</span> and unauthorised structures. A <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">task force</span> led by the municipal authority with the armed services and police was set up to clear canals and enforce disposal rules.

## 8. Courts skipped inmate production after cases of measles at three jails.

Written notices went to benches as remand facilities in <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Colombo, Magazine and Welikada</span> detected infections. A <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">vaccination drive</span> began inside the prisons to contain spread, officials said.

## 9. Regulator kept power tariffs unchanged for the fourth quarter.

The <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">PUCSL (Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka)</span> cited updated cost submissions from the NSO (<span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">National System Operator</span>) showing a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">2.88% uptick</span> in supply costs but left rates at third‑quarter levels after public consultation. The review covered generation mix, fuel prices, capacity costs, BESS (<span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">battery energy storage system</span>) capacity costs and prior revenue adjustments.

## 10. Prosecutors abroad dropped a death‑penalty case against a migrant worker.

Authorities said the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">public prosecution</span> ended all remaining proceedings after a prior appellate ruling had set aside <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">capital punishment</span> but left other penalties. Arrangements were being made for return within <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">one to two weeks</span>, according to officials.
